name: Fix a Deployment that won't go Ready
objective: CKAD › Application Design and Build + Observability. Drill EVERY pod-design corner harder than the exam: classic vs native sidecars, init ordering, all three probe types and handlers, lifecycle hooks + graceful shutdown, full securityContext hardening, QoS classes, the Downward API, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a Deployment that won't go Ready
questions.teach:
To diagnose a pod that's `Running` but never `Ready`, run `kubectl describe pod

` and read **Events** — that's almost always a **readiness probe** pointed at the wrong port/path, so it never answers. Compare the probe target to the port the container actually serves. **Gotcha:** fix the **Deployment** (its pod template), not the pod — then confirm with `kubectl rollout status`.
questions.prompt:
Deployment `diag` in `pod-design` has 1 replica but it **never becomes Ready** (`kubectl -n pod-design get deploy diag` shows `0/1`). Diagnose the fault and fix it so the Deployment reports an available replica. Don't delete and rebuild from scratch — find and fix what's wrong.

Target: Deployment `diag` has at least 1 available replica.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n pod-design describe pod -l app=diag` → the readiness probe is failing. Compare the probe's port to the port the container (`nginx:1.25`) actually serves on. Fix the Deployment's readiness probe (`kubectl -n pod-design edit deploy diag`), then watch `rollout status`.
questions.solution:
# The readiness probe targets port 8080, but nginx serves on 80.
kubectl -n pod-design patch deployment diag --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/port","value":80}]'
kubectl -n pod-design rollout status deployment/diag

verification.description: Deployment diag has >=1 available replica (readiness fault fixed)

questions.eli5:
A detective puzzle with a twist. The pod is **Running** — it's alive — but the Deployment stubbornly shows `0/1` Ready and refuses to send it any customers. Alive but not open for business. Why?

Think of the **readiness probe** as a health inspector who knocks on a specific door and waits for someone to answer "I'm ready!" If someone answers, the inspector flips the sign to Open. The problem: the inspector has been told to knock on **door 8080**, but the shop (nginx) only ever answers at **door 80**. Nobody's behind door 8080, so every knock goes unanswered, the inspector keeps the sign at "Not Ready," and no traffic flows — forever.

The app isn't broken at all; the *check* is pointed at the wrong port. To find this you read the pod's complaint log — `kubectl describe pod` — and the Events show the readiness probe failing (connection refused on 8080). Compare that to the port nginx actually serves (80), and the mismatch jumps out.

The fix: point the probe at **port 80**. But crucially — edit the **Deployment's** pod template, not the live pod. The Deployment is the boss; fix the boss's instructions and it rolls out a corrected pod. Then watch `kubectl rollout status` go green.

**Watch out for:**

- **"Running but not Ready" is almost always a readiness probe failing** — wrong port or wrong path. Read `describe` Events.
- **Fix the Deployment, not the pod.** Editing the live pod gets overwritten; patch `spec.template...` on the Deployment so the change sticks and rolls out.
- **Compare the probe target to the port the container actually serves** — nginx serves 80, not 8080.
- **Confirm with `kubectl rollout status deployment/diag`** — don't assume; watch it report available.
- **Don't delete and rebuild** — diagnose the one wrong field and fix it in place.
questions.deepDive:
## Diagnose & fix: a Deployment that won't go Ready

### Mental model
A container that is **Running but never Ready** almost always has a **failing readiness probe** — the process is up, but the probe's target (port/path/handler) doesn't match what the container actually serves, so it never reports healthy. The Deployment then shows `0/1` available and routes no traffic. Fix the **Deployment's pod template**, not the live pod, so the change persists and rolls out.

### Diagnose
```bash
kubectl -n pod-design get deploy diag                       # READY 0/1
kubectl -n pod-design get pods -l app=diag                  # Running, READY 0/1
kubectl -n pod-design describe pod -l app=diag | sed -n '/Events/,$p'
# Warning  Unhealthy  kubelet  Readiness probe failed: ... connection refused :8080
```
Compare the probe target to the serving port:
```bash
kubectl -n pod-design get deploy diag \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].readinessProbe.httpGet.port}'; echo   # 8080
# nginx serves on 80 → mismatch
```

### Running vs Ready
| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Running` | container process started |
| `Ready` | **readiness probe passing** (or none defined) |
| Deployment `available` | enough Ready replicas for `minReadySeconds` |

Only **Ready** pods receive Service traffic and count toward the Deployment's available replicas.

### Fix (edit the Deployment)
```bash
# targeted JSON patch
kubectl -n pod-design patch deployment diag --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/port","value":80}]'

# or interactively
kubectl -n pod-design edit deploy diag        # change httpGet.port 8080 -> 80

kubectl -n pod-design rollout status deployment/diag        # wait for success
```

### Why edit the Deployment, not the pod
- The Deployment's **ReplicaSet** owns the pods; editing a live pod's probe is overwritten/ignored and lost on the next reconcile.
- Changing `spec.template` triggers a **rolling update** — a new ReplicaSet/pod with the corrected probe.
- `kubectl rollout status` blocks until the new pods are available (or reports failure).

### Common "never Ready" causes
| Cause | Tell |
|---|---|
| Probe wrong **port** | `connection refused` in Events |
| Probe wrong **path** | HTTP 404 in Events |
| `initialDelaySeconds` too low | fails then recovers; flapping |
| App genuinely not listening | app logs show bind error |
| Wrong **scheme** (HTTP vs HTTPS) | TLS handshake errors |

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Running ≠ Ready** — a passing liveness but failing readiness looks "up" yet serves no traffic.
- **Patch the Deployment template**, then `rollout status` — fixing the pod directly doesn't stick.
- **Match probe target to the real serving port/path** — nginx = 80.
- **JSON patch path** indexes the container: `/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/port`.
- **Don't delete/recreate** — the task is diagnose-and-fix in place.
- A readiness failure removes the pod from Service **Endpoints**; check `kubectl get endpoints` to confirm recovery.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n pod-design describe pod -l app=diag | grep -i readiness
kubectl -n pod-design patch deployment diag --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/port","value":80}]'
kubectl -n pod-design rollout status deployment/diag
```
